flashcards.back: The force between two surfaces in contact that opposes their relative slide - which is why it can point forward on a driving wheel.
The single force left after opposing forces are combined: a 60 N push against 40 N of friction leaves a net 20 N.
The turning effect of a force, calculated as force times distance from the pivot, measured in newton-metres.
The fixed point a beam or lever turns around; every moment distance is measured from it.
Force spread over an area, calculated as force divided by area, measured in pascals.
The unit of pressure: one pascal is one newton spread over one square metre.

The push feels the same, so the effect on the ground feels like it should be the same. Pressure is force over area: tiptoes spread the same force over a smaller area, so the pressure is higher. In class, keep the force fixed at 200 N and shrink only the area: 0.5 square metres gives 400 Pa, while 0.05 square metres gives 4000 Pa - the push never changed, only its spread.
flashcards.front: The same push gives the same pressure whether you stand flat or on tiptoes.

flashcards.back: Wrong - the same force now spreads over a smaller area, so the pressure is higher
flashcards.front: A student stands flat, then rises on tiptoes. Her weight has not changed. A classmate says the pressure under her feet is unchanged too. Which statement is correct?
A 30 N weight balances a beam when it sits 1.0 m from the pivot. What moment does it make?

items.answer: Wrong - the same force now spreads over a smaller area, so the pressure is higher
